editorial.copyrightPolicy: Publisher and climbing-media article text is never copied; Swoon'd writes its own explanation and links to the original. Athlete photos, film clips and broadcast video are linked with credit, never assumed redistributable.

masteryModel.usefulCompetenceStatement: Can follow her climbing talk, ask a real question about her project, grade or crag, treat climbing safety with respect, and know when to say 'I'd need an instructor for that', without pretending to be a climber.

licensingConstraints.constraint: Original illustrations and procedural diagrams only (licence id original-swoond). No athlete photos, gym photos or route topos from guidebooks, Mountain Project or social media.
Climbers are named as text. No photos, illustrations of real athletes, or AI likenesses; athlete quotes are not reproduced.
IFSC, Olympic rings, Access Fund, gym chains and gear brands as text only; no logos or branded holds.
No comp, film (Free Solo, Skyscraper Live) or athlete video embedded or re-hosted; link to the rights holder only.

IFSC results and rankings need a licence or written permission before display; no unofficial or scraped APIs (including Mountain Project, theCrag, 27 Crags, Kaya, or IFSC endpoints); those are deep-link only. NWS needs a custom User-Agent; AirNow attribution.
Never copy magazine, news or guidebook text; explain in our own words and link.
Route names, grades and first-ascent facts are facts but each must be checked against a primary source before release; grades quoted as 'graded' rather than asserted.

safetyConstraints: Swoon'd builds appreciation and conversation. It never teaches how to belay, lead, place protection, build anchors, rappel, spot, fall or free solo, and is no substitute for a certified instructor, gym belay test or guide.
Every technique-adjacent lesson says to learn it from a certified instructor or gym, and every decision-scenario carries a safetyNote.
In safety scenarios the cautious option is always best: decline untrained belaying, hire a guide, obey closures, rest injuries, retire doubtful gear. 'Just do it' is never best and never acceptable.
No timers, streak bonuses, speed rewards or leaderboards on safety scenarios; no grade-chasing or 'hardest climb' leaderboards.
Movement vocabulary is recognition only; no body-position coaching, no 'correct beta', no fall technique; the Unity sim shows no climber figure and simulates no movement.
Free solo and extreme feats are admired as culture, never framed as a goal or something to imitate.
No medical advice beyond 'rest and see a clinician if pain persists'; live conditions are informational, never a go/no-go signal, and always link to the land manager.
Safety-critical lessons require a qualified human reviewer (for example a certified climbing instructor or AMGA guide and an Access Fund or Leave No Trace trainer) before release (D-017, P-18).
